source.post_text:
Romero and his camp had continued talks with Arsenal today, they believe that the deal can happen. 

Tottenham are trying their best to stop this being a possibility. 

#THFC

replies.text: Probably is, I’m just speaking hypothetically. £35M is already cheap though, I can’t imagine you’d go any lower
replies.author: @AFC55555

replies.text: Both sides have valid points here really, Arsenal need defensive cover and Romero wants out, yet Spurs are right to protect their asset from a rival so any deal hinges on whether the valuation gap can close reasonably.
replies.author: decoy

replies.text: Trying their best. We literally have him tied down. Could let him rot or sue him into oblivion for breach of contract if he doesn’t anything
replies.author: @GK1Spurs1882

replies.text: I honestly think it will come down to the difference in the bids. If there is only a difference of lets say 5-10m I can't see any scenario Spurs sanctioning it. If the difference is lets say 25-35m then maybe they would look at it as smart business.
replies.author: @Graham_Stewart5

replies.text: He’s already made it clear he won’t play for you again, I think you have no other choice but to sell
replies.author: @Ramseycentro3

decoy_rationale: The reply is oddly balanced and slightly essay-like in neutrally weighing both clubs' positions without a clear partisan edge.
